title: How Justin Welsh built an $8M solo business: niche down, validate 1:1, run a simple funnel
summary: Justin Welsh explains his move from burned-out VP of Sales to a zero-employee business. He covers auditing your time with Pareto, finding a niche, validating by serving 5-10 people one-on-one, using an enemy to build a movement, and a four-step funnel. He also argues for staying specific as an audience grows.

principles.text: Audit your week: rank tasks by impact per hour, focus on the top 20%, and simplify, automate, delegate or eliminate the rest.
principles.quote: you should probably be spending your time doing the 20% of things that maximize 80% of your intended outcome

principles.text: Validate a business by serving 5-10 people one-on-one; if they spend money and time and get results, productize it.
principles.quote: identify five to 10 people who have those problems have those aspirations and want to work with you right and are they willing to put some skin in the game

principles.text: Pick an enemy (an ideology or status quo) to build a movement; marketing works by helping people throw rocks at a common enemy.
principles.quote: once you have an enemy you can build a movement because movements are built by defeating another enemy

principles.text: Keep the funnel simple: get discovered via organic social, build trust with long-form content, deepen relationships for pricey offers, then monetize.
principles.quote: it's get discovered build trust deepen relationships and monetize very simple

principles.text: Stay specific as your audience grows; a niche audience lets you ladder from micro offer to core product to high ticket sooner.
principles.quote: as you grow a specific audience your options are more plentiful right so you can do things like create a micro offer

principles.text: Use AI to analyze your posts, articles and sales data for patterns, and keep the creative work yourself.
principles.quote: keep your creativity let it manage the data
